paper.title_en: Design of a shielding plane for LArPix
paper.abstract_en: The Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE) is a next-generation long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiment. A critical component of the DUNE Near Detector (ND) is a Liquid Argon Time Projection Chamber (LArTPC) called ND-LAr. ND-LAr employs a novel pixelated charge readout based on the LArPix ASIC, enabling native 3D reconstruction through self-triggering pixels. Unlike traditional wire-based readouts, the pixelated anode consists of a single collection plane without induction layers in front. As a result, the pixels can register induction signals from drifting ionization electrons well before they reach the anode surface, leading to pretriggering. To mitigate this effect, we introduce a shielding plane placed above the LArPix anode to confine the signal-sensitive region near the collection electrodes. A 3D field response simulation was developed to optimize the shielding geometry and evaluate its impact on signal formation. We present the shielding plane design and demonstrate its performance using cosmic-ray data collected with a LArPix prototype. The results show improved signal localization and suppression of pretriggering while maintaining high electron transparency.
